title: Land of Loneliness
text:
Land of Loneliness


With time, bodies grow used

to walking completely

        alone

over the land of loneliness.

The vague sensations, the

        memories

of the places where we found

someone with

        whom to speak, someone who would listen

to our words as evening

        falls,

slowly fade away, like

tracks the wind

        extinguishes and disorders.

And the warm echo of the old encounter

does not

        persist in the voice, in the language

with which we learned to name

        things.

Only night remains. And we lose ourselves

in the long silence of

        empty

streets. And when dawn arrives

we feel cold and

        breathe death.

October 16,

        1975
editorial_note: The catalog title differs, but the visible body is 'Land of Loneliness'; this entry preserves the heading and date.

title: Where Did Glory Go, the Feeling
text:
Where did glory go, the feeling

that loved truth, the clear day,

the white cloud, the beautiful thought

full of faith, radiant with joy?


Among the shadow of dark branches

I see the corner of the solitary bed;

there still remains the trace of impure memory,

as though wrapping what the shroud gives.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fragment's mournful question and the dark-bed image despite the source's difficult final phrase.

editorial_note: The translation keeps the linked-pair conceit across dew, perfume, music, stars, and souls.

title: Twin Souls

title: Album of Unknown Origin
text:
Album of unknown origin,

why do you demand my signature?

Signatures and verses from ladies

are things one does not require.

In a woman's life,

inspiration is secret,

like a pale violet

that does not wish to be picked,

and that, when it goes so far

as to exhale a sweet perfume,

should only embalm

the walls of her house.

But making concessions

to this time of madness,

I will alter your whiteness

with uneven lines,

and among signatures of worth

that you already keep with care,

blame your owner

for mine appearing here.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Pardo Bazán's album-verse irony and the period-bound image of domestic modesty.
